data.claim: Splitting the rendered file per top-level table and reading it with read_dropin_dir yields an identical dict and identical Config for every section
data.falsifier: any section differs between layouts, or load over 25 ms
data.mechanism: tomllib per file; merge by table path
data.probe_output: 12 passed incl. every-section equivalence and budget test
data.question: Can one reader load a default.d directory with the same values as the single default.toml, inside the 25 ms budget?

evidence.note: note Re85aaea35e CONFIRMED; measured 9.1 ms for 82 drop-in files vs 5.75 ms single file (budget 25)
r-adapters: read_toml/TomlLibIo reused, no new dependency; no new knob so four-way and upgrade fragment n/a; docs for the user-facing layout land with the split and CFG-docs
12 new tests plus 61 existing pass except size test which is baseline red on main (30,3xx bytes, fixed by the split task)

chunk_findings.detail: `any(PACKAGED_DIR.glob("*.toml"))` treats any filesystem entry matching the pattern as a drop-in file, including directories and broken symlinks. Given `ddflow/templates/default.d/foo.toml/` as a directory (or a dangling symlink named `foo.toml`) and a valid `ddflow/templates/default.toml` containing `[section]` values, the condition is true, so `read_dropin_dir(PACKAGED_DIR)` is used. Since there is no readable TOML file, `read_dropin_dir` will either skip the non-file and return `{}` or fail on it and have the failure caught, resulting in empty packaged defaults instead of falling back to `default.toml`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:61 (`packaged()`)

chunk_findings.detail: When the drop-in directory path is selected and `read_dropin_dir` fails, the warning still references `PACKAGED_DEFAULTS` (`default.toml`) and tells the user to repair with `ddflow pins regenerate --only default-toml`. For example, if `ddflow/templates/default.d/a.toml` has invalid TOML on line 1, the message says the packaged `default.toml` cannot be read and recommends regenerating `default-toml`, which is the wrong file and wrong repair path for a `default.d` parse failure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:65 (`packaged()`)

chunk_findings.detail: In `same_table="error"`, the conflict test `(_defines(val) or _defines(into[key]))` makes a parent table that has an immediate value conflict with a separate file that only adds a sub-table. Given `01.toml` containing `[gate]` / `mode = "strict"` and `02.toml` containing `[gate.a]` / `x = 1`, `read_dropin_dir` raises `DropinError: table [gate] is defined in both 01.toml and 02.toml`. The same content in one `default.toml` is valid TOML and loads both `mode` and `gate.a.x`, and the docstring says sub-tables of a container may be spread over files, so this breaks a packaged drop-in layout that splits a section and its sub-section into separate files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/_layers.py:_merge_into

chunk_findings.detail: `any(PACKAGED_DIR.glob("*.toml"))` treats any glob match as evidence that the drop-in directory “holds files”, but `Path.glob` also matches directories. If `ddflow/templates/default.d/` contains a directory named, for example, `00.toml` and no actual `.toml` files, while `ddflow/templates/default.toml` contains valid packaged defaults, this condition is true. `packaged()` then calls `read_dropin_dir(PACKAGED_DIR)` instead of falling back to `PACKAGED_DEFAULTS`. Depending on the drop-in reader’s file filtering, that call either returns `{}` or raises `IsADirectoryError`, which is caught and results in `{}`; in both cases the valid single-file `default.toml` is skipped and packaged defaults are lost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: When the failure comes from the drop-in directory, the warning still names `PACKAGED_DEFAULTS` as the file that cannot be read. Given `ddflow/templates/default.d/00.toml` containing invalid TOML, the exception may identify `00.toml` and its line, but the message is prefixed with “cannot read the packaged .../default.toml”, which is factually wrong and can misdirect debugging, especially when `default.toml` is absent or unrelated to the failure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:64

chunk_findings.detail: In `same_table="error"` mode the conflict test `_defines(val) or _defines(into[key])` raises when only one file defines the table with a scalar and another file only defines a sub-table. Given `01.toml` containing `[a]` / `x = 1` and `02.toml` containing `[a.b]` / `y = 2`, a single `default.toml` with the same two tables loads, but `read_dropin_dir` raises `DropinError: table [a] is defined in both 01.toml and 02.toml`; the second file does not define table `a` (it is only a container for `a.b`), so the two layouts do not load the same content.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/_layers.py:_merge_into

chunk_findings.detail: `_own` uses dot-joined string paths, so a quoted TOML key containing a dot collides with a nested table path and can make the conflict error name the wrong earlier file. Given `01.toml` `[a.b]` / `x = 1`, `02.toml` `["a.b"]` / `y = 1` (a distinct root table whose quoted key is literally `a.b`), and `03.toml` `[a.b]` / `z = 1`, the first and third files define the same table `[a.b]`; the second file overwrites `owner["a.b"]`, so the error from the third file says the table is defined in `02.toml` and `03.toml` instead of `01.toml` and `03.toml`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/_layers.py:_own

chunk_findings.detail: The new `source = PACKAGED_DIR if dropin_files(PACKAGED_DIR) else PACKAGED_DEFAULTS` line is evaluated before the `try` block, so any `OSError` from probing the drop-in directory escapes `packaged()`. Given a packaged `default.d` directory that exists but is unreadable (for example, mode `000`), `dropin_files` will call `PACKAGED_DIR.is_dir()` and/or `PACKAGED_DIR.glob("*.toml")` and raise `PermissionError`. `packaged()` then crashes instead of catching `OSError`, warning, and returning `{}` as its docstring requires. The previous code performed the `glob` inside the `try`, so moving the directory probe outside the `try` is a regression.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:61 (`packaged()`)

chunk_findings.detail: In `same_table="error"` mode, `_own` records the first file that creates a table path even when that file only creates the path implicitly as a container for a sub-table, and the owner entry is not updated when a later file first adds the table's own values. Given `01.toml` containing `[a.b]` / `x = 1`, `02.toml` containing `[a]` / `y = 1`, and `03.toml` containing `[a]` / `z = 1`, `read_dropin_dir` correctly raises when `03.toml` conflicts with `02.toml`, but the message says `table [a] is defined in both 01.toml and 03.toml`. `01.toml` does not define table `a`'s own values (the change explicitly allows `[a.b]` and `[a]` to live in different files), so the error names the wrong earlier file and can send a user to the wrong drop-in.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/_layers.py:_own
